7th Degree Chords · Level 1.heading: Hear a seventh chord. Choose its type.
7th Degree Chords · Level 1.intro: You will hear four notes played together. Choose the seventh-chord type that matches the sound.

steps.title: Listen to the chord
steps.description: Press Play to hear all four notes together. Listen to the sound they make as a group. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Choose Diminished 7th, Dominant 7th, Minor 7(♭5), Major 7th, Minor 7th. These names describe the different sounds the four notes can make together.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

7th Degree Chords · Level 1.about: A seventh chord has four notes: a three-note chord with a seventh added. For example, F major uses F, A and C; adding E makes F major seventh. “Chord quality” means the chord type. This lesson uses chords built on F. The notes use a close layout, without spreading individual notes into a different high or low range. Choose the chord type only; there is no separate inversion answer. Minor 7(♭5) means minor seventh with a lowered fifth, also called half-diminished.
7th Degree Chords · Level 1.layoutCaption: F major seventh with F at the bottom.
7th Degree Chords · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example is F major seventh. Choose Major 7th. During the quiz, choose the type of chord you hear.

steps.description: First choose the chord type. Then select Root Position, 1st Inversion, 2nd Inversion or 3rd Inversion.
